items_missed: 1_set_agenda: Never asked 'how are you today,' never gave the real agenda statement (what we'll cover + time estimate), never got an explicit 'sound good?'

2_probe: No zip code confirmed, no stairs/floors question despite unloading into a house and garage, no special-considerations question (narrow hallways/tight turns for a 28-ft trailer), no access/parking/HOA question

3_pricing: Only got the 'pricing is super simple' opener and the hourly rate out before the call cut off — no what's-included list, no disassembly/reassembly, no trip fee mention, no No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no no-hidden-fees pitch
4_clock: Section never reached — no clock-start explanation, 2.5-hr minimum, 15-min increments, or sense-check

5_estimate: No formal time-range estimate given; 'two men' was mentioned only as a rate tier, not as a movers/trucks estimate; none of the estimate variables (stairs, specialty items, drive time, etc.) were explained
6_save_your_ass: Entire prep-speech section skipped — no consolidation tips, no carload tip, no close

7_quote_booking: No explicit no-deposit statement, no email handoff explained, no 'any other questions before I let you go,' no hours/contact info given — call ended with 'I'll call you back' and nothing booked
8_politeness: Customer's name ('Amanda') was used only once, short of the 3+ threshold
9_bonus: No rapport/humor moment; insurance (No Worries + 60c/lb) never explained; visible disorganization confirming square footage (bounced between 3000 and 2500)
top_strength: Joanna handled the truck-contents probing carefully (oversized items, specialty items, box count) and proactively answered the customer's floor-covering question well: "we do have flow runners, so we have floor runners... for the guys can definitely bring those as well."
coaching_note: You got the basics — address, size, boxes, oversize-item check — but the call stalled right as you hit pricing, and none of the differentiators, clock, estimate, or booking steps ever happened. When you need to step away to check availability with a manager, say so briefly and then still finish walking through pricing and the next steps before you hang up — don't leave the pitch hanging. Also nail down parking, stairs, and access for a 28-foot trailer unload; that's exactly the kind of job where access issues blow up the clock. Use the customer's name more than once — it was Amanda's whole role to be right there and you called her by name only a single time.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and cooperative but heavily scripted (repeated 'just to confirm' throughout) with minimal warmth or acknowledgment of the customer's firm, no-flexibility date constraint.
audio_review_reason: Several garbled/run-on exchanges (e.g., square footage flip-flopping between 3000 and 2500, incomplete sentences) make it hard to fully judge pacing and tone from text alone.
